questions.question: State the Theorem of Pythagoras in words and in symbols, and say which side is c.
questions.expected_answer: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides: a squared plus b squared equals c squared, where c is the hypotenuse, the side opposite the right angle and the longest side.

questions.question: Explain how squares drawn on grid paper show the theorem for the 3, 4, 5 triangle.
questions.expected_answer: The squares on the legs have 9 and 16 grid squares. The tilted square on the hypotenuse, enclosed in a 7 by 7 square with four triangles of area 6 removed, has area 49 minus 24, which is 25. Since 9 plus 16 is 25, the two smaller squares together equal the largest.

questions.question: A right-angled triangle has legs 6 and 8. Find the hypotenuse, showing the three lines of working.
questions.expected_answer: c squared equals 6 squared plus 8 squared. c squared equals 36 plus 64, which is 100. c equals the square root of 100, which is 10 units.
